lessons.title: Waste produced by three companies
lessons.keywords: Key word: Change over time , Line chart , <4 categories

sections.introduction: The graph illustrates how much waste was produced by three companies over a period of 15 years.
sections.overview: Overall, there was a decline in the amount of waste produced by company A and company B, while an opposite trend was seen in company C. In addition, company A generally had the highest figures throughout the period.
sections.body1: In 2000, the amount of waste produced by company A started at 12 tonnes, after which it experienced a decline to 11 tonnes in 2005. The figure for company B started at 8 tonnes in 2000, before rising to reach a peak at 10 tonnes in 2005. Conversely, the amount of waste for company C started at 4 tonnes, going up to 6 tonnes in 2005.
sections.body2: From 2005 to 2015, the figure for company A continued to decrease, ending the period at 8 tonnes. Similar changes, but to a greater extent, were seen in the figure for company B, which dropped significantly to end the period at 3 tonnes in 2015. Conversely, the amount of waste produced by company C went up significantly to reach the highest point at 10 tonnes in the final year.

lessons.title: Age at first birth
lessons.keywords: Keyword: change overtime, bar chart, >5 categories

sections.introduction: The chart illustrates how many women in six age groups gave birth to their first child between 1966 and 2006.
sections.overview: Overall, there was a decline in the proportion of young mothers under 25, while an opposite trend was seen in the older age groups. In addition, women aged 19-24 consistently had the highest figures in 1966, but they were surpassed by the 30-34 group in the final year.
sections.body1: The proportion of women aged 19-24 started at 62% in 1966, after which it experienced a decline to 36% in 1986, before decreasing to end the period at 28% in 2006. Similar changes, but to a lesser extent, were seen in the figure for the under 19 group, which dropped from 34% in 1966 to 20% in 1986, followed by a final decrease to 12% in 2006.
sections.body2: Conversely, the figure for women aged 30-34 started at 13% in 1966, going up significantly to 18% in 1986, and reaching the highest point at 45% in 2006. A similar upward trend was recorded in the 34-39 and over 40 groups, ending at 30% and 5% respectively in the final year. On the other hand, the proportion of mothers aged 25-30 started at 36%, rose to reach a peak at 50% in 1986, before decreasing to 38% in 2006.

lessons.title: 1.3 · Educational problems — 2 years, table

sections.introduction: The table illustrates how many children experienced different educational problems in two primary schools in 2005 and 2015.
sections.overview: Overall, there was a decline in the proportion of children facing educational problems in School A, while an opposite trend was seen in the figures for School B. In addition, School A consistently recorded the highest figures throughout the period.
sections.body1: Data for the proportion of students with difficulties in following instructions in School A started at 42% in 2005, before decreasing significantly to end the period at 18% in 2015. Similar changes, but to a lesser extent, were seen in the figures for concentration, listening skills, and verbal expression, which dropped to 18%, 20%, and 21% respectively. Conversely, the figures for reading ability and handwriting remained almost unchanged at around 23% and 28%.
sections.body2: The proportion of children experiencing problems with concentration in School B started at 15% in 2005, after which it remained unchanged at 15% in 2015. Similar changes were seen in verbal expression, which saw a slight increase from 14% to 15%. Meanwhile, the figures for spelling and following instructions both doubled to reach 10% and 12% in the final year. Finally, reading ability, handwriting, and listening skills experienced slight rises, ending at 9%, 7%, and 12% respectively.

lessons.title: Cinema attendance
lessons.keywords: Key word: change overtime, line chart, 4 categories

sections.introduction: The graph illustrates how many people in four age groups went to the cinema at least once a month in Great Britain between 1984 and 2000.
sections.overview: Overall, there was an increase in the proportion of cinema-goers in all four age categories examined. In addition, people aged 15-24 consistently recorded the highest figures, while the 35 and over group maintained the lowest figures throughout the period.
sections.body1: The proportion of people aged 15-24 started at 17% in 1984, going up significantly to 55% in 1999, and reaching the highest point at 58% in 2000. Conversely, the figure for the 35 and over group started at only 1% in 1984, before increasing steadily to end the period at 15% in the final year.
sections.body2: The figure for children aged 7-14 started at 10% in 1984, after which it saw a steady rise to reach a peak at 37% in 1999, before decreasing to end the period at 32% in 2000. Meanwhile, the proportion of people aged 25-35 started at 4% in 1984, grew to 25% in 1994, with a subsequent levelling off until 1999, and a final rise to 32% in 2000.

section_labels.body1: Body 1: Nhóm 15-24 và Nhóm 35 and over

lessons.title: Global sales of digital games
lessons.keywords: Key word: change over time, bar chart, 4 categories

sections.introduction: The bar graph illustrates how much money was spent on four types of digital games globally between 2000 and 2006.
sections.overview: Overall, there was an increase in global sales in three categories examined, while an opposite trend was seen in Console Games. In addition, Handheld Games consistently recorded the highest figures throughout the period.
sections.body1: The amount of money spent on Handheld Games started at 11 billion dollars in 2000, going up significantly to 15 billion dollars in 2005, and reaching the highest point at nearly 18 billion dollars in 2006. Conversely, the figure for Console Games started at around 6 billion dollars in 2000, after which it experienced a decline to 4 billion dollars in 2003, before decreasing to end the period at only 3 billion dollars in 2006.
sections.body2: There were no recorded sales for Mobile Phone Games and Online Games in 2000. However, the figure for Online Games started at under 1 billion dollars in 2001, with a subsequent increase to around 6 billion dollars in 2005, and a final rise to 9 billion dollars in 2006. Similar changes were seen in the figure for Mobile Phone Games, which grew steadily to around 3.5 billion dollars in 2004, before rising to end the period at nearly 7 billion dollars in the final year.

lessons.title: New Zealand kiwi fruit exports
lessons.keywords: Key word: change over time, table,  >4 categories

sections.introduction: The table illustrates how much money New Zealand earned from exporting kiwi fruit to five countries between 2010 and 2012.
sections.overview: Overall, there was an increase in the value of kiwi exports to Japan, China, and Russia, while a decline was seen in Mexico and Saudi Arabia. In addition, Japan consistently recorded the highest figures throughout the period.
sections.body1: The amount of money earned from kiwi exports to Japan started at $271,100,000 in 2010, going up significantly to $287,400,000 in 2011, and reaching the highest point at $325,300,000 in 2012. Similar changes, but to a lesser extent, were seen in the figure for China, which grew from $74,900,000 in 2010 to $84,800,000 in 2011, before ending the period at $94,000,000 in the final year.
sections.body2: Regarding the remaining countries, the figure for Russia started at $968,000, after which it experienced a steady rise to $1,585,000 in 2011, before reaching $2,404,000 in 2012. Conversely, export values to Mexico started at $6,000,000, after which it saw fluctuations until 2011, before decreasing to end the period at $3,300,000. A similar downward trend was seen in Saudi Arabia, which rose to $407,000 in 2011, followed by a final drop to $82,000 in 2012.

lessons.title: Parkway Hotel customer service

sections.introduction: The pie charts illustrate how many visitors rated the customer service of Parkway Hotel in two different years, 2005 and 2010.
sections.overview: Overall, there was an increase in the proportion of positive ratings, while an opposite trend was seen in the negative categories over the 5-year period. In addition, "Satisfactory" generally had the highest figures in 2005, but it was surpassed by "Good" in the last year of the period.
sections.body1: The proportion of guests who rated customer service as "Good" started at 14% in 2005, after which it experienced a significant growth to 39% in 2010. Similar changes, but to a lesser extent, were seen in the figure for "Excellent" , which grew from 5% in 2005 to 28% at the end of the period.
sections.body2: Data for "Satisfactory" started at 45% in 2005, before decreasing to end the period at 17% in 2010. Conversely, the figures for "Poor" and "Very poor" ratings also dropped. The percentage of visitors choosing "Poor" decreased from 21% to 12%, while that of "Very poor" fell from 15% to a final 4% in 2010.

lessons.title: 1.8 · Forest industry production — <4 categories, line chart

sections.introduction: The line graph illustrates how much paper, wood pulp, and sawn-wood were produced in the UK from 1980 to 2000.
sections.overview: Overall, there was a significant increase in the production of Paper & Packaging, while a downward or fluctuating trend was seen in the figures for Wood Pulp and Sawn-Wood. In addition, Paper & Packaging generally had the highest figures throughout the period.
sections.body1: The amount of Paper & Packaging started at 230 million tonnes in 1980, after which it saw a slight rise to 250 million tonnes in 1990, before going up significantly to reach the highest point at 350 million tonnes in the final year.
sections.body2: In contrast, the production of Sawn-Wood started at 200 million tonnes in 1980, after which it decreased to 150 million tonnes in 1990, before continuing to fall to 130 million tonnes in 2000. Similarly, changes were seen in the figure for Wood Pulp, which dropped from 170 million tonnes in 1980 to 150 million tonnes in 1990, followed by a slight increase to end the period at 160 million tonnes.

lessons.title: New Zealand population
lessons.keywords: Key word: future, 4 categories , line chart

sections.introduction: The line graph illustrates how many people in four age groups made up the New Zealand population between 1950 and 2050.
sections.overview: Overall, there is a prediction of a decline in the proportions of people aged over 65, 38-45, and 25-37 by 2050, while an opposite trend is expected in the figure for the 0-14 group. In addition, the over 65 category consistently had the highest figures throughout the period.
sections.body1: The proportion of New Zealand population aged over 65 started at around 61% in 1950, after which it experienced a rise to reach a peak at 70% in 1990, before being expected to decrease to 55% in 2050. Similarly, 25% of the people in New Zealand belonged to the 38-45 age group in 1950, with a steady growth to a peak of 48% in 1990, and a prediction of a slight decline to 40% at the end of the period.
sections.body2: The percentage of people aged 25-37 decreased from 21% in 1950 to 10% in 1990, followed by a projection of a continuous drop to nearly 1% in 2050. Conversely, the figure for children aged 0-14 remained relatively stable at around 5% between 1950 and 1990, before being forecasted to increase significantly to 20% in the final year.

section_labels.body2: Body 2 (Khổ nhỏ còn lại: Nhóm 25-37 và 0-14)

lessons.title: Urban populations
lessons.keywords: Key word: future, 4 categories , line chart

sections.introduction: The line graph illustrates how many people in four countries lived in cities between 1970 and 2030.
sections.overview: Overall, there is a prediction of an increase in the proportions of urban population in all four countries examined by 2030. In addition, USA consistently recorded the highest figures throughout most of the period, but it is expected to be reached by Korea in the final year.
sections.body1: The proportion of US citizens living in urban areas started at 70% in 1970, after which it experienced a steady rise to about 88% in 2010, before being expected to reach 90% in 2030. Similarly, 40% of the people in Korea lived in cities in 1970, with a rapid growth to 85% in 2010, and a prediction of a slow rise to 90% at the end of the period.
sections.body2: The percentage of China’s population residing in cities remained stable at 20% from 1970 to 1990, followed by a projection of a continuous growth to about 66% in 2030. Conversely, the figure for India started at 20% in 1970 and grew slightly to 35% in 2010, before being forecasted to increase gradually to around 38% in the final year.

section_labels.body2: Body 2 (Khổ nhỏ còn lại: China & India)

lessons.title: Reasons for migration
lessons.keywords: Key word: No change over time, pie chart

sections.introduction: The pie charts compare the main reasons why people migrated to and from the UK in 2007.
sections.overview: Overall, having a definite job was the primary reason for both immigration and emigration. In addition, formal study accounted for a significantly higher percentage among immigrants than emigrants, whereas looking for work was more common for those leaving the UK.
sections.body1: Regarding immigration, the proportion of people moving to the UK for a definite job was highest, at 30%, followed by formal study (26%). In contrast, accompanying or joining family members stood at 15%, while the figure for looking for work was slightly lower, at 12%. Meanwhile, other reasons and no reason stated accounted for far less of the total, at 11% and 6% respectively.
sections.body2: Looking at emigration, the percentage of people leaving for a definite job (29%) far exceeded that of looking for work and formal study, with respective figures being 22% and 4%. About 18% of emigrants left without stating a reason, compared to 14% for other reasons and 13% for accompanying or joining family. Notably, the proportion of immigrants coming to the UK for formal study was more than six times as high as that of emigrants leaving for the same purpose.

sections.introduction: The chart compares five types of transportation in terms of the numbers of incidents and injuries per 100 million passenger miles travelled (PMT) in 2002.
sections.overview: Overall, Demand Response far exceeded all other categories in both incidents and injuries. In addition, the figures for incidents were consistently higher than those for injuries across all five modes of transport, with Commuter Rail recording the lowest numbers.
sections.body1: Regarding Demand Response, the number of incidents was highest, at 225 per 100 million PMT, followed by injuries at 173. Notably, the figure for incidents in Demand Response was nearly three times as high as that of Bus and Light Rail.
sections.body2: Looking at the remaining transportation types, the figures for Bus and Light Rail were similar in terms of incidents, at 76 each. However, Bus recorded a higher number of injuries than Light Rail (66 compared to 39). Meanwhile, the number of incidents for Heavy Rail was lower, at 51, with its injuries standing at 35. Finally, Commuter Rail was the safest mode, with only 20 incidents and 17 injuries.

lessons.title: Living alone and number of bedrooms

sections.introduction: The bar chart illustrates the proportions of English men and women across various age groups who lived alone in 2011, while the pie chart compares the numbers of bedrooms in these one-person households.
sections.overview: Overall, in the bar chart, living alone was more common among men in younger age groups, whereas women accounted for a higher proportion in older categories. Meanwhile, the pie chart shows that two-bedroom housing was the most popular choice for single occupants, while households with four or more bedrooms made up the smallest figures.
sections.body1: Regarding the bar chart, overall ("All ages"), the proportion of men living alone was lower than that of women, at around 47% compared to 53%. In the younger groups aged 16 to 64, men outnumbered women. Specifically, the percentage of males in the 35–49 age group was highest, at approximately 65%, followed by the 25–34 group at nearly 62%. Conversely, an opposite trend was seen in older categories. Women comprised around 63% of single households in the 65–74 group, and this figure far exceeded that of men in the 85-and-over category, where females accounted for nearly 76%.
sections.body2: Looking at the pie chart, two-bedroom households were highest, at 35.4%, followed by three-bedroom homes at 29.8% and one-bedroom properties at 28.0%. In contrast, large households were much less common. The figure for four-bedroom homes stood at only 5.3%, while five or more bedrooms accounted for far less of the total, at just 1.4%.

lessons.title: Happy Valley shopping centre

sections.introduction: The maps illustrate the changes that took place between 1982 and 2012 in Happy Valley Shopping Centre.
sections.overview: Overall, the shopping centre underwent significant modernization, the most important of which was the removal of the lake to make way for a parking lot and new retail space. In addition, while the central entertainment area remained unchanged, a number of stores were relocated and expanded.
sections.body1: In the western section of the shopping centre, there used to be a lake in 1982, but it was then cleared to make way for a large parking lot and a new furniture retail area. The coffee shop and the old lobby area were demolished, replacing them with a redesigned entrance leading directly into the shopping complex. Meanwhile, no changes were made to the central entertainment area, toilets, and elevators, all of which remained in their original positions.
sections.body2: The northern and eastern parts also saw a number of changes. Along the northern wall, the former food store was replaced by sports and electronics stores, which were relocated from the eastern side. Furthermore, the original furniture store on the east was removed, with a new themed restaurant area being constructed in its place. Finally, the food store was moved to the south-eastern corner of the shopping centre.

sections.overview: Overall, the road network is expected to undergo major developments, the most important of which is the construction of a central roundabout. In addition, traffic lights will be installed at several key intersections to reduce frequent accidents.
sections.body1: In the western section of the map, traffic lights are proposed to be installed at the junction near the school, as well as at the intersections of Low Lane, Forest Road, and City Road. sections.body2: Looking at the central and eastern areas, a large roundabout is forecasted to be constructed at the main intersection, replacing the current dangerous layout. Connected to this roundabout, the northern branch of Forest Road will be realigned to join it directly. Furthermore, two new access roads will be built to link the supermarket directly to the roundabout, with a prediction that the old access point on City Road will be removed.

lessons.title: Making compost

sections.introduction: The diagram describes the process of recycling organic waste to produce fertiliser, also known as compost.
sections.overview: Overall, the process comprises five main steps, beginning with the preparation of a plastic container and ending with the application of the finished compost in the garden.
sections.body1: At the beginning of the process, a plastic container with a volume of two cubic metres is prepared, with holes on its sides to allow air circulation. Next, various organic materials are placed inside the container in layers. A 15-centimetre layer of food is added at the bottom, which is followed by a 15-centimetre layer of grass, a layer of newspaper, and other organic waste on top. Once these ingredients are assembled, nitrogen and a small amount of hot water are poured into the mixture to accelerate the decomposition process.
sections.body2: The process continues with sealing the container using a lid. During this stage, heat is generated inside the container, after which the organic waste is left to ferment over a period of six months. Finally, at the final stage of the process, the organic waste is fully converted into compost, which can then be used to nourish plants in the garden.

lessons.title: Carbonated drinks

sections.introduction: The diagram describes the process of manufacturing carbonated drinks through five distinct stages.
sections.overview: Overall, the process comprises five main stages, beginning with water cleaning and ending with the packaging and transportation of the finished products to supermarkets.
sections.body1: At the beginning of the process, raw water is passed through a filter and a water softener before being treated with chemicals to remove impurities. Once the water is cleaned, it is pumped into electric heaters, which is followed by passing through a cooling pipe. Subsequently, carbon dioxide is added to the water in order to produce carbonated water.
sections.body2: The process continues with the carbonated water being transferred to a mixing tank, where colouring, syrup, and flavouring are added. After the mixture is thoroughly combined, it goes through a filter once again before being filled into bottles or cans. Finally, at the final stage of the process, the packaged drinks are placed into cardboard boxes, after which they are loaded onto trucks and delivered to supermarkets.

Overall, the process comprises a number of steps, beginning with... and ending with...
→ ...beginning with water cleaning and ending with the packaging and transportation...
3. Từ nối (Linking Words):
o At the beginning of the process,...
o Subsequently,...
o The process continues with...
o Finally / At the final stage of the process,...
4. Cấu trúc ngữ pháp quan trọng:
o Before V-ing / S+V → ...before being treated with chemicals... / ...before being
filled into...
o Once S+V , S+V → Once the water is cleaned, it is pumped...
o ... which is followed by V-ing... → ...which is followed by passing through...
o In order to → ...in order to produce carbonated water.
o ... after which S+V ... → ...after which they are loaded onto trucks...
o Thì bị động (Passive voice): is passed, is pumped, is added, is transferred,
are placed, are loaded.
original_paragraphs: Dựa trên hình ảnh sơ đồ quy trình sản xuất nước giải khát có ga (carbonated drinks) gồm 5
giai đoạn chính (Stage 1: Water cleaning, Stage 2: Heating, evaporation and carbonation,
Stage 3: Mixing, Stage 4: Filtering and filling, Stage 5: Packaging), dưới đây là bài viết hoàn
chỉnh targeted Band 6.5 - 7.0.
Bài viết áp dụng chính xác dàn ý, từ nối và toàn bộ các cấu trúc ngữ pháp Process từ bài
trước của bạn:
Dàn ý & Phân tích quy trình (Process)
• Loại bài: Man-made Process (5 giai đoạn đã được gắn nhãn sẵn trên sơ đồ).
• Các giai đoạn chính (Stages):
o Stage 1 (Water cleaning): Nước thô (Raw water) được lọc qua Filter, làm
mềm nước (Water softener), xử lý hóa chất (Chemicals) và bơm (Pump) sang
giai đoạn 2.
o Stage 2 (Heating, evaporation and carbonation): Nước đi qua máy đun điện
(Electric heaters), ống làm mát (Cooling pipe) và được bơm khí Carbon
dioxide để tạo ra Carbonated water.
o Stage 3 (Mixing): Nước có ga được dẫn vào bình trộn (Mixing tank) cùng chất
tạo màu (Colouring), siro (Syrup) và hương liệu (Flavour).
o Stage 4 (Filtering and filling): Nước ngọt sau khi trộn được lọc qua Filter và
đóng vào chai (Bottles) hoặc lon (Cans).
o Stage 5 (Packaging): Sản phẩm được đóng thùng (Drinks boxes) và vận
chuyển bằng xe tải đến siêu thị (Supermarket).
• Bố cục:
o Introduction: Paraphrase đề bài dùng công thức The diagram describes the
process of + V-ing....
o Overview: Công thức Overall, the process comprises 5 main stages,
beginning with water cleaning and ending with packaging and distribution.
o Body 1: Giai đoạn 1 và Giai đoạn 2 (Xử lý nước & Tạo ga).
o Body 2: Giai đoạn 3, 4 và 5 (Pha chế, đóng gói & vận chuyển).
Bài viết hoàn chỉnh (Band 6.5 - 7.0)

lessons.title: Life cycle of salmon

sections.introduction: The diagram describes the life cycle of a salmon from the egg stage to an adult fish.
sections.overview: Overall, the process is a continuous cyclical cycle comprising several distinct stages, which take place in three main environments: rivers, estuaries, and the ocean.
sections.body1: At the beginning of the cycle, adult salmon lay eggs in the river, after which the eggs undergo an incubation period. Once the eggs hatch, young salmon emerge and enter the freshwater rearing stage, where they stay and grow for a period of time. Subsequently, these small fish migrate downstream towards the estuary, at which point they adapt to the brackish water during the estuary rearing phase.
sections.body2: The process continues with the fish migrating further out into the open ocean. During this phase, they move to main rearing areas, where they experience rapid growth and maturation to become fully grown adult salmon. After reaching maturity, the adults begin their journey back to their birthplace in the river in order to spawn. Once the new eggs are laid, the cycle begins all over again.

section_labels.body1: Body 1 (Giai đoạn ở Sông và Cửa sông - River & Estuary)
section_labels.body2: Body 2 (Giai đoạn ở Đại dương & Quay lại đẻ trứng - Ocean & Return)

source_notes: Chi tiết các cấu trúc đã được áp dụng theo yêu cầu của bạn:
1. Thay đổi trong Overview:
o Không dùng ending with... mà dùng Overall, the process is a continuous
cyclical cycle... để nhấn mạnh tính vòng tròn khép kín.
2. Dùng động từ chủ động (Active Voice):
o lay eggs, hatch, emerge, stay and grow, migrate downstream, adapt, move,
experience, reach maturity, begin their journey.
3. Cấu trúc nối câu (Important Structures) được áp dụng:
o ... , after which ... → ...lay eggs in the river, after which the eggs undergo an
incubation period.
o Once S+V , S+V → Once the eggs hatch, young salmon emerge...
o ... , at which point ... → ...migrate downstream towards the estuary, at which
point they adapt to...
o After V-ing / S+V , S+V → After reaching maturity, the adults begin their
journey...
o In order to → ...in order to spawn.
o Once S+V , S+V → Once the new eggs are laid, the cycle begins all over again.
original_paragraphs: Dàn ý & Phân tích quy trình tự nhiên (Life Cycle)
• Loại bài: Natural Process / Life Cycle (Chu trình khép kín, động từ chủ động).
• Các giai đoạn chính:
o Sông (River - Nước ngọt): Trứng (Incubation) → Nở (Emergence) → Nuôi
dưỡng ở nước ngọt (Freshwater rearing).
o Cửa sông (Estuary - Nước lợ): Nuôi dưỡng ở cửa sông (Estuary rearing).
o Biển / Đại dương (Ocean - Nước mặn): Di chuyển đến khu vực nuôi dưỡng
(Migration to rearing areas) → Tăng trưởng và trưởng thành (Growth and
maturation) → Di chuyển ngược lại khu vực đẻ trứng (Migration to spawning
areas).
o Trở lại Sông: Đẻ trứng (Spawning) và chu trình bắt đầu lại.
• Bố cục:
o Introduction: Paraphrase đề bài.
o Overview: Khẳng định đây là một chu trình tự nhiên khép kín (cyclical
process) gồm nhiều giai đoạn diễn ra ở 3 môi trường nước khác nhau (River,
Estuary, Ocean). (Lưu ý: Không viết "ending with").
o Body 1: Các giai đoạn ở Sông và Cửa sông (River & Estuary).
o Body 2: Các giai đoạn ở Đại dương và quay trở lại đẻ trứng (Ocean & Return).
Bài viết hoàn chỉnh (Band 6.5 - 7.0)
